en: The Apadāna of the Elder Kāḷudāyi Bhaddiya Chapter, Number 6 I was once a forest-dwelling sage, a seer named Kaṇhadīpāyana. At that time, the King of Kosala was my friend; he was named Pasenadi. He had a son, Udāyin by name, who was my dear friend as well. Seeing me, he spoke these words: "O Seer, what is your purpose? "I am going to the Himālayas to practice the holy life. Hearing this, he spoke these words: "I too shall go with you. "But, O Seer, I have a duty to perform; I cannot go with you. "Then give me some token, so that I may know you are here. "I shall give you a token, O King's son; you will recognize it. He gave me a golden ring, saying: "This is my sign. When I reached the Himālayas, I practiced the holy life there. Having attained the five supernormal powers, I dwelt in the mountain fastnesses. I was dwelling there when the Blessed One, the Teacher, appeared in the world. Having attained omniscience, he set out toward Benares. Accompanied by a great assembly of monks, he went to Isipatana. There he turned the Wheel of Dhamma; the world was filled with light. Having heard of the appearance of the Buddha, the King of Kosala was delighted. He sent a messenger to the Seer, saying: "Go quickly and bring him back. The Seer, having heard the King’s command, departed from the mountain slopes. He traveled through the air and arrived at Sāvatthī, the city of the King. Standing before the King, he spoke these words: "I have come at your command. The King, seeing the Seer, was filled with joy and spoke these words: "Welcome, O Seer! May you be happy; please accept my hospitality. The Seer accepted the King’s invitation and entered the royal palace. The King, having honored him with food and drink, spoke these words: "O Seer, I wish to see the Buddha; please take me to him. "I shall take you to the Buddha, O King; wait for me here. Having taken leave of the King, the Seer departed through the air. He approached the Blessed One and paid homage at his feet. Standing before the Buddha, he spoke these words: "O Blessed One, the King wishes to see you. The Buddha, knowing the Seer’s intention, consented with silence. The Seer, perceiving the Buddha’s consent, took the King by the hand. He led the King to the presence of the Buddha, the Teacher of the World. The King, having seen the Buddha, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, Was filled with joy and spoke these words: "May the Blessed One accept my hospitality. The Buddha, knowing the King’s intention, consented with silence. The King, having honored him with food and drink, spoke these words: "O Blessed One, I wish to go forth; please grant me ordination. The Buddha, knowing the King’s mind, said: "Come, monk. Instantly, he was shaven-headed and clad in the saffron robes. Having become a monk, he lived in dependence upon the Blessed One. He attained the three knowledges and the six supernormal powers; He became an arahant, free from all taints. The King, having seen the power of the Buddha, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, Was filled with faith and spoke these words:

"I too wish to go forth. The Buddha, knowing the King’s mind, said: "Come, monk. Instantly, he was shaven-headed and clad in the saffron robes. Having become a monk, he lived in dependence upon the Blessed One. He attained the three knowledges and the six supernormal powers; He became an arahant, free from all taints. Thus did the Elder Kāḷudāyi, through his former merit, attain the goal. May all beings be happy and free from suffering. May they find peace and dwell in the bliss of Nibbāna. Thus ends the Apadāna of the Elder Kāḷudāyi.
“The Victor named Padumuttara,
the one with vision regarding all phenomena,
[appeared] one hundred thousand aeons from now.”
In that eon, the Leader appeared—
the Teacher, the best among leaders,
the Victor who knows both virtue and vice.
Grateful and mindful of what has been done,
he established the life-span of beings through his omniscient knowledge.
Having weighed [the matter] with a mind of compassion,
he teaches the sublime Dhamma,
a collection of infinite virtues.
Once, that Great Hero,
wandering in the company of the Conqueror Ananta,
taught the sweet Dhamma.
Having heard that excellent Dhamma, which is connected with the Four Noble Truths and beautiful in its beginning, middle, and end;
There was a realization of the Dhamma by one hundred thousand beings;
at that time, the earth resounded.
The clouds thundered, and the gods,
Brahmās, humans, and asuras raised shouts of "Well done!"
‘Oh, how compassionate is the Teacher!
Oh, how excellent is the teaching of the True Dharma!
Oh, within the ocean of existence!’
The Jina has pulled out [the world] from that which is submerged.
Thus he has proclaimed it among those born—
among humans, gods, and Brahmas.
The Jina praised his disciple as the foremost of those who inspire confidence in the clans.
At that time, in Haṃsavatī, I—
I was born into a family of the dead;
I was pleasing and handsome,
possessing abundant wealth and grain.
Having approached Haṃsārāma and paid homage to that Tathāgata,
I listened to the sweet Dhamma.
And having performed service to the Tathāgata,
I prostrated at the soles of his feet and spoke these words:
"O Sage, he whom you have praised as the foremost of those who inspire faith in the clans—
may I become like him, O Hero."
"In the teaching of the Best of Buddhas";
then the Greatly Compassionate One sprinkled me with his left hand.
He said to me: "Son, arise!
You shall obtain that desire of yours;
how indeed could you fail to pay homage to the Victor?"
Having done so, it would have been in vain.
In a hundred thousand aeons,
one born of the Okkāka clan [will appear].
One named Gotama by clan will become a teacher in the world;
he will be an heir to his teachings.
“Born from the heart, fashioned by the Dhamma,
there will be a disciple of the Teacher named Udāyī.”
Having heard that, being joyful,
I then served the Jina for as long as I lived with a mind of loving-kindness.
[He saw] the Leader, free from conditions.
By that kamma-vipāka and by his volitions and aspirations,
Having cast off the human body,
I went to the realm of the Thirty-three;
and now, in my final existence, I have attained this.
He was born in Kapilavatthu, in the family of a great minister,
to King Suddhodana.
Then Siddhattha was born in the delightful Lumbinī grove for the welfare of the entire world.
And for the sake of happiness, O bull among men.
On that very day I was born,
and I grew up together with him.
A dear companion, beloved,
proficient, and skilled in ethics;
twenty-nine years of age.
Having gone forth from the home life and spent six years,
he became a Buddha, a leader.
Having conquered Māra together with his army,
having exhausted the taints,
and having crossed over the ocean of existence—
The Buddha existed in the world including the devas.
Having gone to the place called Isipatana and having guided the group of five, he taught them.
Then the Blessed One,
having gone here and there, guided those who were ready to be guided.
Guiding those who were to be guided, he—
Gathering in the world with its devas,
the Jina then approached the mountain in Magadha and dwelt there.
Then, sent by King Suddhodana,
the protector of the earth,
I went and saw the One of Ten Powers.
Having gone forth, I became an arahant.
Then, having requested the Great Seer,
I brought him to Kapilavatthu.
Then, having gone there previously,
I inspired confidence in that great family;
the Victor was pleased with that virtue.
In the midst of the great assembly,
the Leader designated me as the foremost of those who inspire confidence in families.
The defilements have been burnt away by me;
I dwell free from taints.
"Welcome indeed has come to me...
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished."
The four analytical knowledges...
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Kāḷudāyī spoke these verses.
This is the sixth legend of the elder Kāḷudāyī.
